4d:T1f38,## Summary

Completes the Flathub-readiness work begun in #7787. That PR added the
`generate-sources.sh` script and wired it into `test-flatpak.yml` so CI
regenerates `node-sources.json` on every run and uploads it as the
`flatpak-node-sources` artifact. This PR finishes the flip:

- **Commits `node-sources.json`** (691 KB, 1202 entries) next to the
  manifest so Flathub's network-less builder can reproduce the install
  offline. Generated against the current `elizaos@latest` (`1.7.2`)
  dependency closure.
- **Flips `ai.elizaos.App.yml`** (direct/power-user variant): the
  `elizaos-app` module now runs `npm install -g --offline --prefix=/app
  --ignore-scripts elizaos`, and `build-options.build-args:
  --share=network` is gone. The build phase no longer needs network
  access, which is exactly what Flathub's submission pipeline requires.
- **Rewrites the long-form comment block** above the `elizaos-app`
  module — the 3-step Flathub-prep playbook from #7787 is no longer
  aspirational; it's how the manifest works today.
- **README**: rewrites the "Flathub submission checklist" step 1 to
  point at the now-automated CI artifact path.

### Bug fix in `generate-sources.sh`

While generating the artifact, hit a real bug in the helper script:
`flatpak-node-generator 0.1.1` crashes with `KeyError: 'name'` when it
parses the root `packages.""` entry of the lockfile, because
`npm install --package-lock-only elizaos@latest` writes a `package.json`
with only a `dependencies` block (no `name` field).

Fix: seed a minimal `package.json` with `"name":
"elizaos-flatpak-sources-shim"` before invoking `npm install`. The
generator now reads the root entry cleanly and emits all 1202 source
records.

Without this fix the CI `Generate offline node sources` step would
silently `continue-on-error`-fail forever and the artifact would never
appear in upload-artifact's output — which is exactly the state we were
in before this PR.

### After this lands

The direct manifest builds with no network access during `build`, which
is the Flathub submission requirement. Next step (separate PR, separate
repo): open `flathub/flathub` submission issue for `ai.elizaos.App`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `Test Flatpak Build` workflow goes green on this PR with the
      committed `node-sources.json` and `--offline` install path.
- [ ] `Generate offline node sources` CI step succeeds (verifies the
      `KeyError: 'name'` fix on the runner's `flatpak-node-generator`
      version).
- [ ] `appstream-util validate-relax` and `desktop-file-validate` still
      pass (already covered by the workflow).
- [ ] `flatpak run ai.elizaos.App --version` still succeeds inside the
      sandboxed build.

Verified locally on WSL Ubuntu 24.04 + Node 18 + `flatpak-node-generator
0.1.1` (uv tool install): script generates 691 KB / 1202-entry
`node-sources.json` against `elizaos@1.7.2` with the fix; crashes
deterministically with `KeyError: 'name'` without it.

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR completes the Flathub-readiness work for the elizaOS App Flatpak by committing a `node-sources.json` manifest (1202 entries, elizaos@1.7.2) and flipping the `elizaos-app` module to a fully offline build.

- **`ai.elizaos.App.yml`**: Removes `--share=network` from build options, adds `npm_config_cache` pointing at the vendored cache, switches npm to `--offline --ignore-scripts`, and correctly references `node-sources.json` as a bare-string include so flatpak-builder processes its archive/script entries rather than treating it as an opaque file.

- **`README.md` + `node-sources.json`**: Checklist and committed source manifest updated to reflect the automated CI workflow and offline build capability.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->4e:T1f0c,## Summary

Brings \`@elizaos/plugin-slack\` from [elizaos-plugins/plugin-slack](https://github.com/elizaos-plugins/plugin-slack) into the monorepo at \`plugins/plugin-slack/\` alongside the other connector plugins already living here (discord, telegram, signal, whatsapp, wechat, xmtp, instagram, matrix, line, feishu, google-chat, imessage, x, twitch, bluesky, bluebubbles, farcaster, nostr).

Slack was the last major-platform connector still living standalone. The standalone repo is at \`v2.0.0-alpha\` with the same \`typescript/python/rust\` layout as plugin-elizacloud and friends, so it was already migration-ready — just hadn't been picked up by the migration sweep.

The source matches the standalone repo's \`next\` branch tip plus the multi-message handling fix from [elizaos-plugins/plugin-slack#1](https://github.com/elizaos-plugins/plugin-slack/pull/1) (\`d50e802\`), which has been sitting on standalone with an APPROVED review since 2026-02-28. That PR will close as superseded by this one.

## What lands

- \`src/\` — service, accounts, formatting, config, index, types, plus:
  - \`actions/\` — sendMessage, editMessage, deleteMessage, listChannels, readChannel, pinMessage, unpinMessage, listPins, reactToMessage, emojiList, getUserInfo (11 actions)
  - \`providers/\` — channelState, memberList, workspaceInfo (3 providers)
- \`__tests__/\` — \`accounts.test.ts\` (98 tests), \`formatting.test.ts\` (22 tests)
- \`package.json\` — workspace-aware: \`@elizaos/core: workspace:*\`, version bumped to \`2.0.0-alpha.537\` to match sibling plugins, scripts aligned with monorepo conventions (biome from root \`node_modules\`)
- \`tsconfig.json\` (modeled on plugin-discord), \`build.ts\` (unchanged from standalone), \`README.md\`, \`LICENSE\`

## API drift fixes (alpha.3 → alpha.537)

The standalone \`peerDependencies\` pinned \`@elizaos/core: 2.0.0-alpha.3\`. The monorepo is at alpha.537, and the core API has moved in two specific ways the slack plugin needed updates for:

- **\`State.recentMessagesData\` typing.** Providers in \`channelState.ts\`, \`memberList.ts\`, \`workspaceInfo.ts\` read \`state?.recentMessagesData\`, which is now typed as the broader \`StateValue\` union (\`string | number | bigint | true | object\`) rather than \`Memory[]\` directly. Cast the field to \`Memory[] | undefined\` at the read site so \`validateActionKeywords\` / \`validateActionRegex\` get the expected shape. Behavior unchanged.
- **\`MentionContext\` shape.** \`service.ts\` was constructing \`{ isMention: true }\`; the type now requires \`isReply\` and \`isThread\` too. Filled with \`false\` for the mention-only path. Behavior unchanged for the existing mention handling.

## Verified

- ✅ \`tsc --noEmit -p plugins/plugin-slack/tsconfig.json\` clean
- ✅ 120/120 unit tests pass (\`bun test plugins/plugin-slack/__tests__/\`)
- ✅ \`bun run build.ts\` produces \`dist/index.js\` + \`.d.ts\` cleanly

Large. This touches Cloud app auth, app-scoped chat, Cloudflare domain management, and container deployment status handling. Review should focus on route ownership checks, billing/error behavior, and deployment lifecycle state transitions.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds the production Cloud path needed for agent-built monetized apps:

- App-scoped chat endpoint support at `/api/v1/apps/:appId/chat`, routed through the configured provider/AI Gateway with app monetization metadata.
- Cloudflare-managed app domain support, including check/buy/status/sync flows and app-domain ownership checks.
- App auth callback/session handling needed for generated apps to complete OAuth-style sign-in and return to the app.
- Local container control-plane deployment support and immediate monitor reconciliation so a healthy container is marked `running` instead of staying stuck in `deploying`.
- Skill docs aligned with the Cloud container/OAuth/monetized-chat/domain lifecycle.

## What kind of change is this?

Features and bug fixes.

# Documentation changes needed?

Updated included skill documentation for Cloud app builds and app domain lifecycle behavior.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

Start with Cloud app/domain route changes, then the container deployment status monitor, then the skill docs.

## Detailed testing steps

- `bun run --cwd cloud/apps/api typecheck`
- `bun run --cwd cloud/services/container-control-plane typecheck`
- `bun test cloud/packages/tests/unit/domains/domain-pricing.test.ts cloud/packages/tests/unit/domains/cloudflare-dns-stub.test.ts cloud/packages/tests/unit/domains/cloudflare-registrar-stub.test.ts`
- Local Discord e2e with normal app prompts spawned Codex, registered Cloud apps, enabled app-scoped monetized chat, completed OAuth-style app auth, offered Cloudflare domains, and verified unsigned chat returns `401 not_signed_in`.
- Local custom-domain e2e verified `nubilio.org` against the local Cloud stack and confirmed the app auth entry point returns Cloud HTML.

# Deploy Notes

Requires the Cloud API/frontend/control-plane deploy together. Configure Cloudflare registrar/DNS env vars and the AI Gateway/provider env already expected by Cloud. Container deployment status depends on the container control-plane service being reachable.

## Database changes

Includes Cloud domain/app-domain state changes from the Cloud codepath. Run the Cloud migrations before enabling the new domain/app routes in prod.

Deploy Cloud API, frontend, and container control-plane from the same revision. Do not enable automatic domain purchase without the existing user confirmation step.

This PR adds the production Cloud path for agent-built monetized apps: app-scoped chat at `/api/v1/apps/:id/chat` with credit debit/reconcile, Cloudflare-managed domain buy/check/status/sync/verify flows, an app OAuth-style auth callback, and a new Node container control-plane sidecar with an immediate deploy-monitor reconciliation on container creation.

- **P1 — Auth errors return 500 on the chat endpoint:** `requireAuthOrApiKeyWithOrg` is called inside `Promise.all`. For API-key callers (where the global middleware skips validation), any `AuthenticationError` or `ForbiddenError` is caught by the outer catch and returned as HTTP 500 instead of 401/403.
- **P1 — Sync never marks a Cloudflare domain as `verified` after zone provisioning:** When a domain is purchased while zone creation is still pending (`verified: false`), calling `/sync` later sets `status: \"active\"` but omits `verified: true`, leaving `listVerifiedAppOrigins` (used for CORS) permanently empty for that domain.

53:T6fab,# Relates to

- Follows the architecture work from #7779.
- Accounts for #7844: upstream is collapsing the old Satellite/Carrot vocabulary into remote-mode Plugins (`mode: "direct" | "remote"`). This branch accepts the landed remote-plugin naming and keeps the implementation compatible with that direction.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This PR makes the iOS app and remote coding path usable from mobile while preserving the new remote-plugin architecture boundary.

- Adds the iOS local voice/onboarding path around the full Bun/native local-inference lane.
- Moves mobile onboarding toward a simpler cloud/sky visual treatment with fewer cards, smaller radii, and clearer voice/download state.
- Uses Kokoro/mobile TTS for onboarding greeting instead of blocking first-run on OmniVoice warmup.
- Keeps local voice asset readiness separate from engine readiness so the UI does not claim synth success before a real probe works.
- Carries the remote coding/sandbox work so mobile can route coding sessions to Eliza Cloud or home/remote workers instead of trying to run Codex/Claude/OpenCode/PTYs inside the iOS App Store client.
- Keeps `plugin-coding-tools` parity scoped: `ls` can route through `eliza.fs`; grep/glob remain plugin-owned until explicit search/glob semantics exist; edit remains plugin-owned until a first-class patch/edit capability exists.
- Reconciles the branch with latest `origin/develop`, including the Babylon -> Feed rename and the upstream remote-plugin vocabulary changes.

## Why is this needed?

The product goal is that a user can open Eliza on a phone and still use the agent to talk, set up local voice/model state, sign into cloud, and start real coding work from any device. iOS cannot safely or App-Store-compatibly run arbitrary PTYs, Codex/Claude/OpenCode agent runners, or native build tools inside the client. Those jobs need to route to an Eliza Cloud sandbox or a trusted home/remote worker, while the mobile app stays the controller and renderer.

This PR also removes ambiguity around voice readiness. Having the files on disk is not the same as having a working native synth engine, and onboarding should not pretend otherwise.

# Risks

Medium. This touches mobile onboarding, iOS local voice, capability routing tests, and the remote-plugin merge boundary. The riskiest areas are native iOS voice/runtime behavior on physical devices and CI paths that moved under the recent `develop` rename wave.

# Documentation changes needed?

Docs are included where this branch already introduced or updated the remote coding/sandbox and mobile paths. No separate migration guide is required for app users in this PR.

## Context

Fixes the root cause behind the May 2 `CACHE_ENABLED=false` hotfix:
`CacheClient` was a module-level singleton whose lazy-opened Redis socket
got bound to the first request's I/O context on Cloudflare Workers,
killing the worker on subsequent requests with `Cannot perform I/O on
behalf of a different request`.

Rather than just fix the cache singleton (étape 2 plan, ALS facade with
documented dette), the user chose **Clean Architecture** (étape 3) — no
intermediate dette, layered domain/application/infrastructure, repository
pattern, cache as decorator. See ADR:
[docs/architecture/clean-architecture-migration.md](cloud/docs/architecture/clean-architecture-migration.md).

## Architectural concession (validated 2026-05-03)

The clean DI / `c.var.deps` pattern applies to the **Hono request scope**.
For elizaOS plugin runtime services (`N8nCredentialBridge`),

  Mitigated by a regression test that hammers steward-session.56:T257d,## Summary

Adds `@elizaos/plugin-gitpathologist` — a per-surface forensic git-history analyzer for elizaOS agents.

- **What it does:** scans `git log` for a path/glob surface, classifies each commit (conventional-commit rules), scores per-commit health deltas + a running EMA, finds peaks (local health maxima) and drift inflections (commits after which the score sustains a downturn), and writes a post-mortem `RotCause` for each drift.
- **Pipeline shape:** deterministic spine (`scan` → `classify` → `score` → `inflect`), LLM only for `narrate`, with a deterministic fallback when no `runtime.useModel` is available. All commit text + diff snippets pass through a local secret scrubber (`sk-ant-`, `sk-`, `ghp_`, `AKIA`, `Bearer`, env-name patterns) before leaving the process.
- **API:** single multiplex `GIT_PATHOLOGY` action with operations `report` (default), `list`, `trace` (v2 stub), `diff` (v2 stub). Reports cached to `<repo>/.milady/gitpathology/<sha256(surface+since)>.json`, freshness keyed on HEAD sha.
- **Wiring:** added to `OPTIONAL_CORE_PLUGINS`, gated by `gitpathologistRequested()` alongside the orchestrator gate. Resolution order: config agent entry → defaults → `ELIZA_GITPATHOLOGIST` env var → auto-on when `<cwd>/.git` exists. Mobile platforms never load it. `gitpathologist?: boolean` added to `AgentEntryConfig`, `AgentDefaultsConfig`, and both zod schemas.

## Why

Forensic "when did this surface look best, when did it veer off, and why" analysis is something every long-lived monorepo needs and nobody has a clean plugin for. `plugin-github` covers PR/issue ops, not commit-history pathology. This fills that gap with cheap deterministic detection and optional LLM narration — pairs naturally with spatial codebase tools.

## Test plan

- [x] **Unit + e2e:** 45/45 vitest pass in `plugins/plugin-gitpathologist/`. Coverage: `secret-scrubber`, `classify` (conventional + WIP + revert + merge + risk flags), `score` (deltas, EMA, revert-proximity penalty), `inflect` (peaks, drifts, threshold filtering), `cache` (key stability, round-trip, freshness), `scan` (real git output via toy-repo fixture), full pipeline e2e on a synthetic A(clean)→B(WIP dump)→C(churn-spiral)→D(recovery) repo.
- [x] **Typecheck:** `tsc --noEmit` clean for the plugin (same 5 pre-existing `@elizaos/core` codegen errors as plugin-mcp's baseline — not introduced by this PR).
- [x] **Dogfood:** Ran [`scripts/dogfood.ts`](https://github.com/2-A-M/eliza/blob/milady/plugin-gitpathologist/plugins/plugin-gitpathologist/scripts/dogfood.ts) against `packages/agent/src/runtime` over a 60-day window. 119 commits scanned in ~160ms, 5 plausible peaks and 3 plausible drift inflections detected, including a 31,403-line "chore: restore current develop tree" correctly flagged as the largest drift.
- [ ] **Future:** v2 `trace` (symptom → introducing-commit walk) and `diff` (compare two surfaces / windows) operations; LLM-batch classify pass to refine "other" → real category on non-conventional commit subjects.

## Out of scope for v1 (deliberate)

- Cross-surface dependency graph (Understand-Anything territory)
- PR-level aggregation (commit-level is the load-bearing primitive)
- Author-level metrics (privacy/political minefield, no clear use case)
- Auto-fix suggestions (this plugin diagnoses; coding plugins prescribe)
- Web dashboard (JSON + markdown is enough for v1)
- Sub-agent fan-out per surface (sequential single-process is fine until profiling proves otherwise)

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

Introduces `@elizaos/plugin-gitpathologist`, a new optional plugin that performs forensic git-history analysis for a path/glob surface, producing a scored health timeline, peak/drift inflection detection, and an LLM-narrated (or heuristic-fallback) rot post-mortem. It wires into `OPTIONAL_CORE_PLUGINS` and auto-loads when the workspace contains a `.git` directory.

- **Pipeline:** deterministic spine (`scan` → `classify` → `score` → `inflect`) with LLM only in the `narrate` phase, capped by a configurable `budget`; all commit text and diff snippets pass through a local secret scrubber before leaving the process.
- **Integration:** `gitpathologist` boolean added to `AgentEntryConfig`, `AgentDefaultsConfig`, and both Zod schemas; a `gitpathologistRequested()` gate respects config → env-var → auto-detect precedence and excludes mobile platforms.
- **Cache:** reports stored as JSON under `<repo>/.milady/gitpathology/`; `read()` and `list()` still call `JSON.parse` without a try/catch (flagged in prior review round).

<h3>Confidence Score: 4/5</h3>

Safe to merge once the unguarded JSON.parse calls in the cache layer are addressed; the rest of the pipeline is well-structured and self-contained.

The cache's read() and list() methods still call JSON.parse without a try/catch, meaning a single corrupted cache file throws through runReport() and crashes the analysis instead of falling back gracefully.

plugins/plugin-gitpathologist/src/cache/report-cache.ts — unguarded JSON.parse in both read() and list() is the outstanding concern from the prior review round.

<h3>Important Files Changed</h3>




| Filename | Overview |
|----------|----------|

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR wires up ERC-8004 on-chain agent identity registration on BNB Chain by adding a viem-based `ERC8004IdentityClient`, four new Hono route handlers (register, current identity, URI update, on-chain lookup), a Drizzle `agent_identities` schema, and Steward policy gating.

- `POST …/register` encodes `register(agentURI)` calldata, asks Steward to sign and broadcast, waits for the receipt, parses the `Registered` event, and persists the identity record in the DB.
- `PUT …/uri` and `GET …/onchain` follow the same auth + Steward policy pattern; `GET …/identity` is a pure DB read.
- The `agent_identities` schema is intentionally migration-less here (Track 1A dependency) and protected by a 503 guard if the table is absent at runtime.

<h3>Confidence Score: 3/5</h3>

Not safe to merge without addressing the reverted-transaction handling and the TOCTOU registration race; both can silently leave the system in an inconsistent state between on-chain state and the DB.

The register and URI-update routes never inspect `receipt.status`, so a reverted on-chain transaction causes the code to proceed into event-parsing, fail with a generic 500, and — in the URI route — may write the new URI to the DB even though the chain still holds the old value. There is also no coordination primitive between the existence check and the on-chain broadcast, meaning two concurrent requests can each mint a token and only the first DB insert survives, leaving an orphaned on-chain identity. The `getAgentId` method adds a second `waitForTransactionReceipt` with no timeout after the first (60-second) call already confirmed the tx, which could hang on a flaky node. These three issues all live on the critical registration path.

`register/route.ts` and `uri/route.ts` need the revert-check and race-condition fixes before going to production; `identity-client.ts` should be updated to accept an optional pre-fetched receipt in `getAgentId`.

   <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=9" align="top"></a> **TOCTOU race allows double on-chain registration**

   There is no lock between the `getCurrentIdentity` existence check and the on-chain `register` transaction. Two concurrent POST requests for the same `agentId` + `chainId` will both find `existing === null`, both pass the policy gate, and both broadcast a `register` call to the contract — minting two separate token IDs and charging gas twice. The second `dbWrite.insert` then fails on `agent_identities_sandbox_standard_chain_unique`, so the caller gets an error even though an on-chain identity was created. The orphaned token has no DB record.

   Consider taking a DB advisory lock (e.g. `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock`) keyed on `(organizationId, sandboxAgentId, chainId)` before issuing the on-chain transaction, or using an `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` with a pre-insert rather than a read-then-write pattern.


2. `packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/erc8004/identity-client.ts`, line 2144-2167 ([link](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/blob/658319478ec0163d07b8c18f1b3300d17d681fa5/packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/erc8004/identity-client.ts#L2144-L2167)) 

   <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=9" align="top"></a> **`getAgentId` calls `waitForTransactionReceipt` a second time with no timeout**

   In `register/route.ts`, `waitForTransactionReceipt` is already called (with `timeout: 60_000`) before `getAgentId` is invoked, yet `getAgentId` issues its own `waitForTransactionReceipt` call with no `timeout`. If the RPC node hasn't indexed the receipt yet (rare but possible on load-balanced nodes), this second call can hang indefinitely. The logs decoded inside `getAgentId` come from this second receipt, not from the one used to obtain `blockNumber`, creating a subtle divergence.

   Consider accepting an optional `receipt` parameter so callers that already have the confirmed receipt can skip the second RPC round-trip.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->58:T1507,## Summary

Adds a deterministic pre-deploy validation+repair pass that closes 10 distinct LLM-hallucination classes before the workflow ever hits n8n. Five-commit chain (kept as separate commits on this branch for review traceability — happy to squash on merge if preferred).

This is the largest of the four anti-hallucination PRs and the one with the highest production impact. With this pass enabled, our hit rate on **one-shot, no-manual-fixes workflow generation** went from \"often needs manual edits\" to \"works on first try for the canonical Gmail→Discord, RSS→Slack, scheduled-summary patterns\" — verified across hundreds of dogfood runs.

### Hallucination classes closed

1. **typeVersion outside catalog** — clamped to the highest valid `typeVersion ≤ requested`.
2. **typeVersion outside actual n8n runtime** — intersect catalog ∩ live `/types/nodes.json`.
3. **`/types/nodes.json` multi-entry merge** — Gmail/Discord listed once per versioned-node class; Set-accumulate across same-name entries (fixes a `flatMap` bug that picked the first entry's versions only).
4. **Missing `parameters.authentication`** when credentials attached — back-fill from `displayOptions.show.authentication`.
5. **Output-field references with case mismatches** — deterministic case-fix against the upstream node's actual output schema.
6. **Bracket-notation expressions `\$json[\"X\"]`** — regex extended to catch the bracket form, not just dot-notation.
7. **Aggregation-source-field hallucinations** — Summarize node's `field` parameter validated against the upstream source node's output schema.
8. **Static-schema vs runtime-shape mismatch** — Gmail simple-mode override beats static schema (node returns flat fields when `format: simple`, deeply-nested when `format: full`).
9. **Node-name collisions** — auto-rename with `(N)` suffix.
10. **Connection edges to non-existent nodes** — drop + log.

### What's new

- **`src/utils/validateAndRepair.ts`** (561 lines) — the orchestrator. Walks every node, runs each validator, applies repairs in-place. Returns `{ workflow, repairs: [], errors: [] }`. Pure function — no n8n calls.

- **`src/utils/inferSyntheticOutputSchema.ts`** (144 lines) — when an upstream node has no static output schema, infer one from its `parameters.fieldsToOutput` or similar. Used by the case-fix and aggregation-source validators.

- **`src/utils/api.ts`** (48 lines added) — `/types/nodes.json` parsing fix: aggregate `typeVersion` arrays across all entries with the same `name`, instead of taking the first entry's.

- **`src/utils/catalog.ts`** (47 lines added) — `clampTypeVersion(node, runtimeVersions)` helper.

- **`src/utils/outputSchema.ts`** (16 lines added) — exported helper for case-folded field lookup, used by the validator.

- **`src/utils/generation.ts`** (77 lines added) — \"catalog facts\" block injected into the prompt: per-node-type, lists allowed `typeVersion`s and required parameters. Helps the model produce correct workflows on first generation, reducing repair work.

- **`src/services/n8n-workflow-service.ts`** (92 lines added) — wiring: call `validateAndRepair` after generation, inject repair feedback into a retry prompt if errors remain, retry up to N times. Backs off cleanly if all retries still have errors and surfaces the residual error list to the host.

- **`src/prompts/workflowGeneration.ts`** (45 lines added) — instructional rules added to the prompt explaining each anti-hallucination invariant in plain English (model accuracy improves measurably when the rule is also stated in the prompt, not just enforced post-hoc).

- **`__tests__/unit/validateAndRepair.test.ts`** (503 lines, all new) — covers each of the 10 hallucination classes plus the retry loop wiring. Pure unit tests — no live n8n required.

### Why a deterministic pass

The repair-via-LLM-retry path alone has three failure modes:
- It's slow (extra round-trips, often two or three).
- The model sometimes \"fixes\" the wrong thing (changes a node type when the issue was just a typeVersion).
- It can introduce new hallucinations while fixing the old ones (cycle).

A deterministic pass with the catalog + runtime as ground truth is faster, cheaper, and has a bounded blast radius. Repair-via-LLM still runs **after** the deterministic pass for residual errors the deterministic pass can't fix on its own.

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR stabilizes the gpt-oss/OpenCode live path by tightening several planner and routing contracts: it adds malformed Stage 1 tool-call recovery, throttles/deduplicates autonomy drain tasks, preserves a single tool's exact `userFacingText` over evaluator paraphrase, adds configurable sub-agent progress policy (compact/threaded/silent with a startup delay), and restores Discord reply references for TASKS-spawned bot messages.

- **Core planner changes** (`planner-loop.ts`, `action-tiering.ts`, `message.ts`): `preferredFinalMessageFromToolOrModel` now prefers a single successful tool's `userFacingText` over the evaluator's synthesized reply; Stage 1 retry logic is extended to catch malformed (present-but-empty) `HANDLE_RESPONSE` tool calls; canonical action names are registered before similes to prevent simile-based capture of real action surfaces.
- **Orchestrator + Discord** (`plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/index.ts`, `plugin-discord/service.ts`): Sub-agent progress delivery is gated by a configurable delay and mode policy, clearing timers on `task_complete`/`task_error`; Discord reply references are now propagated through `originConnectorMessageId` so final bot messages reply to the triggering prompt; `sub-agent-router.ts` adds verify-retry event suppression and makes `requireFresh` opt-in so files pre-dating a session start are no longer treated as dead URLs.
- **Infrastructure** (`task-drain.ts`, `batcher.ts`, `dispatcher.ts`, `plugin-sql/base.ts`): Duplicate persisted drain tasks are deleted on startup; recurring batcher sections are throttled by `minCycleMs`; `agentId` is added to `getTasksByName`/`getTask` return shapes needed by `matchesTask`.

<h3>Confidence Score: 4/5</h3>

Safe to merge with minor cleanup; all changes are well-tested and address real live-trajectory issues observed in production.

The three flagged issues are all non-blocking: a dead `chunks.length === 1` condition in the Discord multi-chunk path (doesn't affect the final reply behavior), a `shouldRun` predicate evaluated after the recurring-section timestamp is already advanced (potential over-suppression in niche section configs), and a redundant `typeof serialized === "string"` guard in `isUnsupportedCancelError`. None introduce incorrect behavior in the primary live paths. The core behavioral changes — Stage 1 retry extension, tool-text priority, action-tiering canonical-first registration, delay-based progress gating, and verify-retry suppression — are all clearly intentional, consistently tested, and address concrete trajectory failures observed in live runs.

`plugins/plugin-discord/service.ts` for the dead condition in the multi-chunk send path; `packages/core/src/utils/prompt-batcher/batcher.ts` for the mark-before-shouldRun ordering.

   <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=8" align="top"></a> `_markRecurringSectionAttempt` is called before the `shouldRun` predicate is evaluated. If `shouldRun` returns `false` (e.g., "no pending work yet"), the timestamp is still advanced, so the section will be suppressed for the full `minCycleMs` window even though it never produced any model output. For sections that combine `shouldRun` with a long `minCycleMs`, this can delay the first actual execution if the predicate flips to `true` shortly after a skipped cycle.

<details><summary><h3>Greptile Summary</h3></summary>

This PR adds a Swift-specific RPC bridge (`POST /api/swift/rpc`) that maps named method envelopes to existing elizaOS REST routes, migrates the macOS client to use it exclusively, and implements a full native chat flow with conversation lifecycle management, queued prompts, and a runtime-readiness polling loop.

- **RPC bridge** (`swift-mac-rpc-routes.ts`): validates method names against a static allowlist, translates params to existing route calls, and forwards the upstream response in a typed `{ok, status, result}` envelope; the upstream URL is constructed from the incoming `Host` header, creating an SSRF exposure.
- **RuntimeController** (`RuntimeController.swift`): adds pipe-based stdout/stderr capture and a synchronous preflight script that blocks the `@MainActor` thread until the node process exits, which will freeze the UI.
- **AppModel** (`AppModel.swift`): implements queued chat, conversation lifecycle, and a 30-second readiness polling loop; contains a private helper `refreshRuntimeSetupSnapshot(after:)` that is defined but never called.
</details>


<h3>Confidence Score: 3/5</h3>

Two issues need to be resolved before merging: the RPC bridge builds its upstream URL from the untrusted Host header (SSRF), and the preflight script blocks the main actor thread synchronously, freezing the macOS UI on first launch.

The RPC bridge introduces an SSRF path where a forged Host header redirects proxy calls to arbitrary addresses. Separately, the synchronous waitUntilExit() call inside @MainActor-isolated ensureRuntimePreflight will stall all UI updates for however long the node code-generation script takes to run. Both are present defects on code paths that execute on every cold start and every RPC call.

swift-mac-rpc-routes.ts (SSRF in forwardRPCRequest) and RuntimeController.swift (blocking main actor in ensureRuntimePreflight) are the two files that need changes before this is safe to ship.

<details open><summary><h3>Security Review</h3></summary>

- **SSRF via `Host` header** (`packages/agent/src/api/swift-mac-rpc-routes.ts`, `forwardRPCRequest`): The upstream URL is assembled from the untrusted `Host` request header. A request with a crafted header (e.g., `Host: 169.254.169.254`) causes the bridge to proxy to that address. Fix: hardcode `127.0.0.1` and derive the port from the server socket.
</details>

<!-- /greptile_comment -->5b:T33de,> **Note**: this PR supersedes [#7808](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/7808), which was auto-closed when the branch was renamed (\`feat/orchestrator-http-server\` → \`feat/agent-lifecycle-via-job-queue\`). The first three commits (\`d29da4c\`, \`fb1a92b\`, \`7f670b9\`) are identical to what reviewers saw on #7808 — including the Greptile findings and the fix commit \`7f670b9\`.

## Architectural shift

**Cloudflare Workers never talk to Hetzner cores directly.** Every cores-bound op flows through the job queue, the orchestrator daemon (the only context with SSH keys + a stable outbound network identity) executes it, and the Worker reads the result from \`jobs.result\`.

Previously the Worker code path called \`elizaSandboxService.shutdown()\` / \`provision()\` / \`snapshot()\` / bridge-HTTP-fetch inline. SSH-bound calls silently no-op'd from Workers; bridge-HTTP calls failed for stopped or crashed agents (no bridge to fetch from). Result: DB rows that claimed \`stopped\` while containers kept burning RAM, "save snapshot" 500s, and a logs view that returned empty for any non-trivially-running agent.

## Scope (all shipped in this PR)

Six lifecycle operations, five new job types, six route rewrites. Pattern mirrors the shipped \`agent_delete\` (PR #7746).

| Op | Job type | Daemon executor | Route(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Suspend | \`AGENT_SUSPEND\` | \`executeSuspend\` — SSH \`docker stop\`, DB→stopped, keeps sandbox_id | \`PATCH /v1/eliza/agents/[id]\`, \`POST /v1/eliza/agents/[id]/suspend\`, \`POST /v1/agents/[id]/suspend\`, \`POST /compat/agents/[id]/suspend\` |
| Resume | \`AGENT_RESUME\` | \`executeResume\` → \`provision()\` (URLs + DB restored) | \`POST /v1/eliza/agents/[id]/resume\` |
| Restart | \`AGENT_RESTART\` | \`executeRestart\` — shutdown + provision atomic | \`POST /v1/agents/[id]/restart\` |
| Logs | \`AGENT_LOGS\` | \`executeLogs\` — SSH \`docker logs --tail N\` via \`provider.fetchLogs()\` | \`GET /v1/agents/[id]/logs\`, \`GET /compat/agents/[id]/logs\` |
| Snapshot | \`AGENT_SNAPSHOT\` | \`executeSnapshot\` — daemon-side snapshot() | \`POST /v1/eliza/agents/[id]/snapshot\` |

## Greptile-resolved (from #7808, commit \`7f670b9\`)

The fast-path \`docker start\` in \`executeResume\` was dead code on \`DockerSandboxProvider\` (no standalone \`start()\` exposed), so every resume already paid the full re-provision cost. Greptile flagged three derived issues: bridge_url not restored, no lifecycle lock, silent fallback. Fix: drop the fast path. \`provision()\` restores URLs and holds its own advisory lock. Real fast path returns when the provider grows a \`start(sandboxId): Promise<SandboxHandle>\` — tracked as follow-up.

## What I tested

**Locally:**
- [x] \`tsc --noEmit\` clean on cloud-shared (touched files filtered)
- [x] biome check clean on all 10 touched files
- [x] \`bun test packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/__tests__/provisioning-job-types.test.ts\` → 4 pass, 100% coverage on the registry file. Catches typos / missing entries / duplicates / non-snake-case.
- [x] Manual /clean single-pass on the diff: no slop, no defensive overkill, no \`any\` / \`as unknown\` casts. JSDocs explain Why.

**What I did NOT test (needs deploy on both Worker + daemon VM):**
- [ ] e2e dashboard: each of suspend / resume / restart / logs / snapshot via the dashboard against a live agent
- [ ] Idempotency: rapid double-click on any op → second returns existing job
- [ ] Logs job uniqueness: completed logs job is NOT reused on a fresh click (only in-flight ones are)
- [ ] \`/api/v1/jobs/<id>\` polling surfaces status transitions correctly

**Test gap:**
The \`execute*\` methods aren't unit-tested. cloud-shared has no harness for mocking \`dbWrite.transaction\` + advisory locks + SSH provider. Same gap as the shipped \`agent_delete\` / \`agent_provision\` paths. Follow-up of its own size.

## Frontend UX note

Snapshot / suspend / restart toasts fire optimistically (the same as today for the already-shipped suspend route): the user sees "Snapshot saved" before the job actually completes. The DB eventually reflects reality. To make the toast truthful, the frontend needs to extend its existing \`poller.track(agentId, jobId)\` flow (used today for provision/resume) to cover the new 202 paths. Follow-up frontend PR.

## Follow-up

- Frontend poller for the new 202 routes (suspend, restart, snapshot, logs) — kills the optimistic-toast lie.
- Real fast-path \`docker start\` via \`provider.start()\` returning a fresh handle (perf optimization, ~5s vs ~60s for resume).
- DRY the now-seven \`enqueue*Once\` methods — ~80 LOC of near-identical lock + idempotency code per method. Touches shipped code, so out of scope here.
- Test harness for the execute* methods (covers this PR + the existing \`agent_delete\` / \`agent_provision\` paths).
- 5 remaining \`elizaSandboxService.shutdown()\` callers from non-route contexts (\`agent-managed-github\`, \`agent-managed-discord\`, \`eliza-managed-launch\`, \`active-billing\`). Architectural question: should those services run as Workers or daemon? Same Worker-side gap applies.

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR shifts all agent lifecycle operations (suspend, resume, restart, logs, snapshot) from inline Cloudflare Worker calls to a job-queue pattern executed by the daemon — the only context with SSH access to Hetzner cores. It adds five new job types mirroring the shipped `agent_delete` pattern, rewrites six route handlers to return `202 + jobId`, and implements five daemon-side `execute*` methods in `ElizaSandboxService`.

- **Six route rewrites** across `v1/`, `v1/eliza/`, and `compat/` replace direct `elizaSandboxService` calls with `provisioningJobService.enqueue*Once` + `triggerImmediate()`, returning `202` and a polling envelope.
- **Five new `execute*` methods** in `eliza-sandbox.ts` handle the actual SSH operations daemon-side: `executeSuspend` (advisory-locked transaction), `executeResume` (delegates to `provision()`), `executeRestart` (sequential `shutdown` + `provision`), `executeLogs` (SSH `docker logs`), and `executeSnapshot` (delegates to existing `snapshot()`).
- **`DockerSandboxProvider.fetchLogs`** is added with integer-clamped `safeTail` and `2>&1` stderr merge so crashed agents' boot traces are included.

<h3>Confidence Score: 4/5</h3>

The structural change is sound — six routes correctly shifted from inline Worker calls to job-queue dispatched by the daemon — but the `triggerImmediate()` calls without CF Worker env bindings mean the orchestrator kick is a no-op at runtime, so jobs sit pending until the next cron tick.

The `triggerImmediate` / missing env-binding issue carried from the prior review is a present runtime defect: the daemon wake-up call silently fails in every new route that adds the pattern, so suspend, restart, logs, and snapshot operations will always incur the full cron-tick latency rather than the near-instant dispatch intended.

The `triggerImmediate()` calls across the new route handlers (restart, suspend, logs in `v1/agents/`, PATCH in `v1/eliza/agents/[agentId]/route.ts`, and the newly added resume/snapshot/suspend under `v1/eliza/agents/`) all need the `c.env` pass-through addressed before deploy.

<h3>Sequence Diagram</h3>

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant W as CF Worker (route)
    participant DB as Database (jobs)
    participant D as Daemon (orchestrator)
    participant H as Hetzner Core (SSH)

    C->>W: "POST /suspend | /restart | /snapshot"
    W->>DB: "enqueue*Once() advisory lock, idempotency check, INSERT job"
    DB-->>W: "job {id, status: pending}"
    W->>D: triggerImmediate() best-effort
    W-->>C: "202 {jobId, polling.endpoint}"

    Note over D: Cron tick or triggerImmediate kick
    D->>DB: SELECT pending jobs
    DB-->>D: job row

    alt AGENT_SUSPEND or AGENT_RESTART
        D->>H: SSH docker stop container
        H-->>D: ok
        D->>DB: "UPDATE status=stopped, bridge_url=NULL"
    else AGENT_RESUME
        D->>H: provision() docker run + health check
        H-->>D: bridgeUrl, healthUrl
        D->>DB: "UPDATE status=running, bridge_url, health_url"
    else AGENT_LOGS
        D->>H: SSH docker logs --tail N
        H-->>D: stdout+stderr
    else AGENT_SNAPSHOT
        D->>H: fetch bridge_url/snapshot
        H-->>D: backup metadata
        D->>DB: INSERT agent_sandbox_backups
    end

    D->>DB: "UPDATE jobs SET status=completed, result"
    C->>DB: "GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} poll until completed"
    DB-->>C: "{status, result}"
```

<!-- greptile_failed_comments -->
<details><summary><h3>Comments Outside Diff (1)</h3></summary>

1. `packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/provisioning-jobs.ts`, line 936-957 ([link](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/blob/e8f60f9765a3bf8a44848d297701dcd89642909c/packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/provisioning-jobs.ts#L936-L957)) 

   <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=8" align="top"></a> **Idempotency key for `AGENT_LOGS` ignores the `tail` parameter**

   The in-flight dedup query matches any `pending`/`in_progress` `agent_logs` job for the same agent, regardless of `tail`. A second request for `tail=5000` while a `tail=100` job is executing returns the `tail=100` job, but both route handlers respond with the caller's own `tail` value in the envelope. The client sees `alreadyInProgress: true` but the job stored in `jobs.data.tail` and eventually written to `jobs.result.tail` is 100 — clients polling the job will receive 100-line logs when they asked for 5000. Either include `tail` in the idempotency check, or make the response tail field come from the returned job's data rather than the caller's parameter.
</details>

<!-- /greptile_comment -->5c:T2d1c,P1 of the **Plugin/mode unification**, stacked on PR #7844.

Where P0 added the vocabulary, manifest schema, and wire-envelope types, **P1 makes remote-mode plugins actually run**: a worker bootstrap, a host-side bridge that mirrors worker surfaces into the agent runtime, and an isolated-process worker runner so plugins requesting `isolation: \"isolated-process\"` no longer silently downgrade.

## Commits

| Commit | Scope |
|---|---|
| `feat(plugin-worker-runtime): scaffold worker bootstrap for remote-mode plugins` | New package `@elizaos/plugin-worker-runtime`. Worker-side bootstrap: imports the author's Plugin object, walks surfaces, announces, dispatches inbound `worker-rpc`. Modules: `envelope` (WorkerChannel + Worker postMessage adapter), `error` (Error round-trip with boundary marker), `runtime-proxy` (RuntimeProxy + buildRuntimeProxyApi for the subset of IAgentRuntime remote plugins call), `descriptor` (Plugin → JSON announce), `dispatch` (`worker-rpc` → live handler), `bootstrap` (entrypoint). |
| `feat(agent): RemotePluginBridge — host-side wiring for remote-mode plugins` | New `packages/agent/src/services/remote-plugin-bridge.ts`. On `worker-announce-plugin`, materialises a stub `Plugin` with handlers that proxy to the worker via `worker-rpc` and registers it via `runtime.registerPlugin(...)`. Inbound `host-rpc` from the worker is dispatched against the real `IAgentRuntime` (getService / useModel / getMemory / createMemory / updateMemory / emitEvent / getSetting / setSetting / composeState). |
| `feat(electrobun): IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner — Bun.spawn for isolation:isolated-process` | `SubprocessWorkerHandle` (newline-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout, stderr inherits to host log, SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL termination with 2s grace). `IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner` + `AdaptiveWorkerRunner` (picks per-plugin between Bun-Worker and Bun-subprocess based on `permissionsGranted.isolation`). Default `RemotePluginHost` now uses the adaptive runner; the warn-and-fallback path is deleted. Worker side gets `createSubprocessChannel()` + `createDefaultChannel()` (env-sniffs `ELIZA_REMOTE_PLUGIN_CHANNEL=stdio`). |

## Surfaces wired in P1

| Surface | Worker side (dispatch.ts) | Host side (RemotePluginBridge) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | ✅ | ✅ | Pure JSON in / out |
| `event` | ✅ | ✅ (fires on worker via `worker-rpc`, listens via `host-rpc emitEvent`) | Pub/sub both directions |
| `model` | ✅ | ✅ | JSON in / out; streaming via `stream-chunk`/`stream-end` lands in P2 |
| `action` | ✅ (callback no-op) | ✅ (callback param dropped) | Action `validate` round-trips via `worker-rpc` too. Full callback marshalling is P1.5 |
| `evaluator` | ✅ | n/a in P1 bridge (TBD next iteration) | Worker dispatcher handles inbound invocations |
| `route` | ✅ (path through) | deferred to P2 | Routes need agent HTTP server registration + SSE/multipart handling |
| `service` | rejected with typed error | n/a | P2 with explicit `static rpcMethods` opt-in |
| `views`/`widgets`/`componentTypes` | passed through as JSON | passed through to existing views registry | The agent's `/api/views/:id/bundle.js` already supports `bundleUrl` for remote plugins, so no new code needed |

## Isolation

- `isolation: \"shared-worker\"` (default) → Bun `Worker`. Cheap, shared crash domain.
- `isolation: \"isolated-process\"` → `Bun.spawn`. Crash domain isolated. Required for sub-agent plugins (Claude Code, Codex, opencode runners) and any plugin with `bun.process: true`.

The wire envelope is identical in both cases — switching is a channel-construction choice, not a protocol fork.

## What's still TODO

- **Action callbacks** (P1.5): worker-side `CallbackProxy` whose invocations round-trip to the host's real `callback` via `worker-rpc surface=\"action.callback\"`. Most action handlers either don't use callback or rely on the orchestrator's progress channel today.
- **Service surface** (P2): explicit `static rpcMethods: string[]` opt-in, then `ServiceProxy` synthesis.
- **Route surface** (P2): agent HTTP server registers stubs; SSE + multipart support; 25MB body cap for remote routes.
- **View-host shim packages** (P2): `@elizaos/plugin-host-shim-{electrobun,ios,android,web}` — ~50 LOC each, all conform to the `PluginHostShim` contract.
- **`runtime.installRemotePlugin(...)`** (P3): agent-generated plugin pipeline with inline source delivery + permission narrowing.

## Verify

Skipped on the worktree (no `bun install`); CI on this PR will validate. The two key invariants are:
1. A `Plugin` with `mode: \"remote\"` reaches the runtime as a normal-shaped Plugin object via the bridge.
2. A subprocess-based worker can complete the announce → dispatch → result round-trip over stdio with the same envelope the Worker channel uses.

## Base branch

Stacked on `shaw/p0-plugin-mode-unify` (PR #7844). Merge order: P0 first, then P1 rebases automatically. If P0 is reshaped, P1 needs a rebase pass — most P1 code is new files so conflicts will be in `agent/services/index.ts` and `agent/package.json` only.

This PR introduces P1 of the plugin/mode unification: a new `@elizaos/plugin-worker-runtime` package (worker-side bootstrap, descriptor builder, RPC dispatcher, transport adapters, error serialization), a host-side `RemotePluginBridge` that materialises stub plugins from worker announce descriptors, and an `IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner`/`AdaptiveWorkerRunner` pair that honours `isolation: "isolated-process"` via `Bun.spawn` instead of silently falling back.

- **New package `@elizaos/plugin-worker-runtime`**: Worker bootstrap walks plugin surfaces, registers handlers in a local registry, announces descriptors to the host, and enters a steady-state RPC dispatch loop; transport is abstracted over a `WorkerChannel` interface with implementations for both Bun Worker postMessage and subprocess stdio.
- **`RemotePluginBridge` (host side)**: On `worker-announce-plugin` it synthesises action/provider/event/model stubs whose handlers proxy back via `worker-rpc`, and dispatches inbound `host-rpc` calls against the real `IAgentRuntime` — including an unrestricted `setSetting` that warrants a permission gate.
- **`IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner`**: Spawns a fresh `bun` subprocess per isolated-process plugin using newline-delimited JSON over stdio; the `AdaptiveWorkerRunner` default picks between Bun Worker and subprocess based on the plugin manifest's `isolation` field, but currently forwards all host environment variables to the subprocess.

<h3>Confidence Score: 3/5</h3>

The core announce-before-init ordering bug means the host can invoke worker handlers against an uninitialised plugin, and the process.env spread and unrestricted setSetting create security exposure that is easy to overlook since isolated-process mode is specifically designed for higher-risk code.

Three distinct defects span the two most security-sensitive paths in the PR: all host environment variables are forwarded to subprocess workers, defeating the confidentiality goal of process isolation; remote workers can overwrite arbitrary host-runtime settings without a permission check; and the worker announces before its init completes, opening a window where dispatched handlers run against uninitialised state.

- **`IsolatedProcessWorkerRunner` (`remote-plugin-host.ts` line 297)**: Spreads `...process.env` into every isolated-process subprocess. All host secrets (API keys, database credentials, tokens) are forwarded to what is explicitly intended to be an untrusted/sandboxed process.
- **`setSetting` host-rpc handler (`remote-plugin-bridge.ts` lines 464–468)**: Any remote worker can call `runtime.setSetting(key, value)` with an arbitrary key and value. <!-- /greptile_comment -->5f:T2d70,P0 of the **Plugin/mode unification** decided in the architecture-review v3 thread on PR #7779. Closes the open question of what to call the abstraction PR #7779 was inventing: **everything is a Plugin**, with a single `mode: \"direct\" | \"remote\"` field.

This PR is the bandaid-rip: rename, collapse vocabulary, ship the type spine. Behavior of all existing direct plugins is unchanged (`mode` defaults to `\"direct\"`).

## What's in P0

| Commit | Scope |
|---|---|

## What's NOT in P0 (P1+ work)

- Actual surface-parity for remote-mode plugins (`actions`/`providers`/`services`/`models`/`events`/`routes`/`views`) — the wire envelope types are in place, dispatch comes in P1/P2.
- Deletion of `RuntimeBrokerCapabilityRouter` standalone class.
- Deletion of `RemoteCapabilityRouterService` standalone Service.
- `Bun.spawn`-based `isolation: \"isolated-process\"` implementation (today's `RemotePluginHost` silently downgrades to `shared-worker` — known TODO).
- View-host shims for iOS / Android / web (Electrobun shim becomes one of four).
- `runtime.installRemotePlugin(plugin, ...)` API for agent-authored plugins.

See the architecture review for the full phased plan.

## PR #7779

Disposition: rebase after this lands. Take the renames as given; re-roll the six \"satellites/\" directories as `mode: \"remote\"` Plugin objects; delete the `dynamic-views/` parallel registry (use the existing `views` field with `bundleUrl`); rename `coding-satellite/` → generic `remote-plugin-host/` cloud container. <!-- /greptile_comment -->60:T11a0,## Summary

Stabilizes the Linux desktop local-source startup path after the recent local-inference and renderer changes.

- Trusts live Electrobun/API boot progress in the renderer startup coordinator so the UI can leave `STARTUPSHELL.STARTING` once the API child is actually running.
- Keeps the Linux voice pill disabled by default and gates it behind `ELIZA_DESKTOP_PILL`, avoiding the duplicate loading-window surface on startup.
- Moves the pill shell to a minimal early mount path when explicitly enabled.
- Routes renderer imports through browser-safe local source entries for `@elizaos/ui` / `@elizaos/app-core`, reducing stale npm/dist and server-only barrel leakage.
- Syncs cloud public assets before desktop renderer builds and serves cloud media with correct MIME types.
- Defers the local-inference `TEXT_EMBEDDING` handler until a real Eliza-1 backend is active, so startup no longer aborts on embedding warmup before model activation.
- Adds missing package export subpaths and route-plugin specifiers needed for source-mode app/plugin loading.
- Adds tests for boot config bridging, crypto readiness, pill gating, renderer static assets, startup restore/runtime behavior, core plugin ordering, native module stubs, and i18n keys.

## Root Cause

The Linux desktop app had multiple startup races layered together:

1. In external dev/API mode, Electrobun could report a stale local `not_started` boot state even while `/api/health` already reported `agentState: running`, leaving the renderer stuck on the startup shell.
2. The desktop pill path created a second renderer surface by default and previously loaded the full app bundle before reaching the pill-only branch.
3. The renderer could resolve package roots through broad barrels or stale dist/npm package paths instead of local browser-safe source entries.
4. Local inference statically registered `TEXT_EMBEDDING` before a local backend was active, so startup probes could claim an embedding provider that could not serve yet.

<h3>Confidence Score: 4/5</h3>

Safe to merge with one fix: the EventSource client needs an onerror handler to prevent infinite reconnect loops when the task is deleted or returns a non-2xx response.

The SSE client in `streamOrchestratorTask` has no `onerror` handler. When the server returns a 404 (task not found or deleted) or any other error, the browser's EventSource automatically retries every ~3 seconds indefinitely, hammering the endpoint until the component unmounts. The polling fallback is already in place, so simply closing the EventSource on error loses no functionality. Everything else — the conversation builder, diff renderer, stop/Esc bar, cross-task contamination fix, and auto-spawn path — looks correct and well-guarded.

packages/ui/src/api/client-agent.ts — the `streamOrchestratorTask` function needs an `onerror` handler that calls `source.close()`.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->65:T23fa,## Summary
Wire up a real fleet rollout for cloud agents. When the registry-side digest of the configured agent tag moves, the daemon now enqueues a blue/green \`agent_upgrade\` job per running agent still on the old digest, capped at 3 in flight, and executes them as zero-downtime cross-node swaps.

Today's reality: a new image only reaches the fleet when an agent crashes or someone restarts it manually, so the cluster runs a mix of versions until everyone naturally cycles. The morning of 2026-05-29 had agents on \`develop\` alongside agents on \`eliza-tla:patched\` for that reason.

## How it works
- **Probe**: the reconciler calls \`resolveImageDigest(containersEnv.defaultAgentImage())\` against ghcr.io every 30s. Cached 60s. Null on bare image names, non-ghcr registries, or registry errors — those cycles are no-ops, the agent stays put.
- **Pick a target node**: \`getAvailableNode({ excludeNodeId: currentNode })\`. Different node guarantees no container-name collision (names are deterministic \`agent-\${id}\` per docker daemon). Autoscaler-on-demand path fires automatically if no other node has free capacity.
- **Provision blue + health check**: regular provisioner path with the new image. If it never goes healthy, we tear down blue and bail — the agent keeps running on old with old image. Auto-rollback.
- **Atomic swap**: one UPDATE on \`agent_sandboxes\` (bridge_url, health_url, node_id, container_name, ports, docker_image, image_digest). New HTTP requests hit blue from this point on.
- **Drain + remove old**: \`docker stop -t 30\` SIGTERM (30s drain for in-flight HTTP + websockets), \`docker rm -f\`. Allocated count decremented on the old node.
- **Cleanup**: the autoscaler's existing idle-node drain handles nodes that empty out as agents rebalance.

## Schema
New \`image_digest text\` column on \`agent_sandboxes\`, stamped at provision time. NULL on rows that predate this PR is treated as "differs from target" — first rollout sweeps the existing fleet onto the current digest, after which the registry-vs-stored compare is exact.

Migration 0135, additive, no backfill required.

## Test plan
- [x] 17 unit tests on the registry probe — parsing edge cases (port-in-registry, bare image names, empty tag, malformed), 404 / 5xx / network-error handling, only-ghcr policy, positive + negative caching with TTL expiry verification.
- [x] Smoke test on the job-type registry — \`AGENT_UPGRADE\` is registered and unique.
- [x] \`biome check\` clean on all changed files.
- [x] \`typecheck\` clean for the changed files.
- [ ] Manual end-to-end on staging: push a fresh \`:develop\`, watch the reconciler enqueue + execute 3 swaps per cycle, verify blue boots healthy, swap is atomic, old container gets a SIGTERM drain.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)
- Per-agent opt-out flag (some agents may need to be pinned to a digest).
- Idle-aware scheduling (skip swap when an agent has an active websocket).
- Webhook from \`build-agent-image.yml\` to trigger an immediate rollout rather than waiting for the 30s reconciler tick.

   <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=9" align="top"></a> **Overcommit risk when old-node SSH is unreachable**

   `decrementAllocated` runs unconditionally after the stop/rm attempts, even if both fail (e.g., a network partition to the old node). If the SSH calls throw and the container stays alive, `allocated_count` on the old node is decremented past its real container count. Subsequent scheduling decisions will treat that node as having more free capacity than it actually has, and the next agent provisioned there can exceed the node's actual limits. The autoscaler's idle-drain will eventually reconcile, but the gap can span multiple reconciler cycles on a busy fleet.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->66:T3215,## What this does

Makes a provisioned container the actual inference target for an agent. Before this change the live reply path ran the agent in-process in the gateway worker and the provisioned container was never routed to (orphaned compute). After this change inbound platform messages are forwarded to the container that hosts the agent, and the container boots as its assigned character.

- **Container self-registration.** When a provisioned container boots, the in-container runtime writes two keys to the shared sandbox registry (Upstash REST): `server:<name>:url` (the container's reachable URL) and `agent:<characterId>:server` (the agent-to-server pointer). The keys carry a short TTL that a periodic refresh renews while the container is alive; if the container dies the keys expire and the gateways stop routing to a dead address. A graceful shutdown deletes the keys when they still point at this container.
- **Boots as the assigned character.** The container reads its injected character (`ELIZA_AGENT_CHARACTER_JSON`) and its routing id (`SANDBOX_ROUTE_AGENT_ID`) and boots as that character instead of the bundled default preset. The runtime agent id is pinned to the platform character id so the gateway lookup and the `/agents/<id>/message` address both resolve to this container.
- **Gateway routes via the registry.** `gateway-discord` resolves a registered container's URL from the registry and forwards inbound messages there. When no registry key exists for an agent it falls back to the existing in-worker path, so currently-working in-worker agents are unaffected. The container-route path is effectively feature-flagged by the presence of the registry key.
- **Service-to-service auth.** The gateway attaches an `X-Server-Token` header (the shared service secret) on the forwarded request, and the container accepts it. This mirrors the existing agent-server contract and lets the gateway authenticate without knowing the per-agent inbound API token.
- **Connector ownership.** Connectors are gateway-owned by default. A container can opt in to owning its own connectors with `ELIZA_SANDBOX_OWNS_CONNECTORS=1`; otherwise the container strips connector bot tokens at boot so it does not double-connect the same bot token the gateway is already holding.
- **Removes the Kubernetes scale assumption.** The gateways run on Railway, not Kubernetes, so the route path no longer PATCHes a Kubernetes Deployment to scale a server up.

## Security properties

- `X-Server-Token` is honored only when `AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET` is set and non-empty. When the secret is unset the header carries no authority, so there is no auth regression for any deployment that never configures it (fail-safe when unset).
- The token comparison is constant-time (`crypto.timingSafeEqual` after a length check).
- The gateway attaches the token only when its own copy of the secret is present in env.
- Self-registration only fires when the full set of sandbox registry env vars is present, so it is inert on every non-provisioned runtime.

## Rollout requirements

This change is inert until the deploy is configured for it. To turn it on:

1. Set `AGENT_SERVER_SHARED_SECRET` to the same value on both the gateway (gateway-discord) and the provisioning daemon that launches containers, so the gateway-attached `X-Server-Token` matches what the container expects.
2. Rebuild and reprovision the container image so containers run this code (self-registration plus character boot plus `X-Server-Token` acceptance).
3. Ensure the sandbox registry credentials (`KV_REST_API_URL` / `KV_REST_API_TOKEN`, surfaced to the container as the `SANDBOX_REGISTRY_*` env) are set so containers can self-register and the gateways can resolve them.

If any of these is missing the system falls back to the existing in-worker behavior with no regression.

## Tests

New unit tests cover the inbound `X-Server-Token` auth path, the sandbox registry self-registration/refresh/unregister logic, and the character loader. All touched-package unit tests pass.

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR wires provisioned Hetzner containers as the real inference target for agents: containers self-register in a shared Upstash Redis registry on boot, the `gateway-discord` resolves that registry entry before forwarding inbound Discord messages, and a service-to-service `X-Server-Token` header authenticates the forwarded request.    <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=9" align="top"></a> **Missing `model` (and other `AgentConfig` fields) from injected character**

   `applySandboxCharacterFromEnv` builds the entry with personality fields (`bio`, `system`, `style`, etc.) but does not copy `model`, `skills`, `humanDelay`, `identity`, `tools`, or `groupChat` from the parsed character JSON. If the database record for this agent has a specific model configured (e.g. `"openai/gpt-4o"`) or has a restricted skills list, those values are silently dropped and the container boots with the runtime's default model and full skill set instead. This defeats the stated goal of booting the container "AS its assigned character" — the persona is right but the inference target and capability set may not be.


2. `packages/agent/src/runtime/sandbox-registry.ts`, line 838-855 ([link](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/blob/e2ecd61a5320ad4731a0ada339d3a0c21a0f03f7/packages/agent/src/runtime/sandbox-registry.ts#L838-L855)) 

   <a href="#"><img alt="P2" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p2.svg?v=9" align="top"></a> **TOCTOU window in `unregister()` during rolling deploys**

   `unregister` reads both keys, decides which to delete, then issues a `DEL`. Between the two `GET` calls and the `DEL` a new container could claim one key (but not yet the other) — e.g. `agent:X:server` gets updated to the new sandbox while `server:old:url` is still this container's. In that window the `registeredServer !== serverName` guard would skip the agent key (correct) but the URL check would still pass and `DEL server:old:url` would remove the new container's live route, causing a brief 90-second outage for that agent until its TTL or next heartbeat recovers it. Consider using a Lua script or a Redis transaction to make the conditional DELETE atomic.

</details>

## The four host-shim packages

| Package | Wire | URL scheme |
|---|---|---|
| `@elizaos/plugin-host-shim` (contract + web/XR iframe) | `parent.postMessage` → dashboard / xr-view-host | `/api/views/<name>/<path>` |
| `@elizaos/plugin-host-shim-electrobun` | `globalThis.__elizaosElectrobunBridge` (preload) | `views://<name>/<path>` |
| `@elizaos/plugin-host-shim-ios` | `window.webkit.messageHandlers.elizaosBridge` (WKScriptMessageHandler) | `app-resource://plugin/<name>/<path>` |
| `@elizaos/plugin-host-shim-android` | `window.ElizaosAndroidBridge` (@JavascriptInterface) | `https://appassets.androidplatform.net/plugins/<name>/<path>` |

Identical PluginHostShim contract:

```ts
interface PluginHostShim {
  resolveViewUrl(pluginName: string, relativePath: string): URL;
  request<T>(method: string, params: JsonValue): Promise<T>;
  on(event: string, handler: (data: JsonValue) => void): () => void;
}
```

Author usage in a view bundle:

```ts
import { installElectrobunShim } from \"@elizaos/plugin-host-shim-electrobun\";
installElectrobunShim();
import { getHostShim } from \"@elizaos/plugin-host-shim\";
const result = await getHostShim().request(\"provider.spotify\", {});
```

The platform-specific install is the only line that differs across platforms.

## Service opt-in

A remote-mode service must declare `static rpcMethods: string[]`. Methods NOT in that list are invisible to the host — preventing accidental over-exposure of private state. The worker side has a per-class lazy instance cache so the service starts once, on first invocation, with the worker's RuntimeProxyApi.

```ts
class MyService {
  static serviceType = \"my-service\";
  static rpcMethods = [\"ping\", \"compute\"];
  static async start(runtime) { return new MyService(runtime); }
  async ping() { return \"pong\"; }
  async compute(x: number) { return x * 2; }
  // private internals: invisible to the host
}
```

## Route stubs

Route handlers in a remote-mode plugin author-declare with the standard `Route` shape (legacy `handler(req, res)` not supported in remote mode — must use `routeHandler(ctx)`). The bridge synthesises a stub whose `routeHandler` forwards `RouteHandlerContext` via `worker-rpc surface=route` and returns the `RouteHandlerResult`. The agent's existing plugin-route lifecycle picks the routes up and registers them on the HTTP server.

SSE / multipart support uses the wire envelope's `stream-chunk`/`stream-end` messages (declared in P0); full plumbing through the bridge lands in a P2 follow-up. Today's bridge handles non-streaming routes end-to-end.

## What's still TODO

- Action callbacks (P1.5 — host marshals callback() invocations back to its real callback via `worker-rpc surface=\"action.callback\"`).
- SSE / multipart in route stubs.
- Evaluator stubs in the bridge.
- `runtime.installRemotePlugin(plugin, source)` API (P3).

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR delivers the P2 layer of the plugin/mode unification stack: four platform-specific `PluginHostShim` packages (web/XR iframe, Electrobun, iOS, Android) that give remote-mode view bundles a uniform `request`/`on`/`resolveViewUrl` surface, plus wiring for the two remaining hard surfaces — `service` (opt-in via `static rpcMethods`) and `route` (non-streaming, `routeHandler`-only).

- **Host shims** (`plugin-host-shim`, `-electrobun`, `-ios`, `-android`): Each ~120-LOC package implements the same `PluginHostShim` contract; only the native bridge call differs per platform.
- **Service surface** (`descriptor.ts`): A module-level `WeakMap` lazily starts services on first RPC invocation and caches the instance; `rpcMethods` act as an explicit allowlist so private state is never reachable from the host.
- **Route surface** (`remote-plugin-bridge.ts`, `dispatch.ts`): `makeRouteStub` synthesises a `routeHandler` that serialises `RouteHandlerContext` over worker-rpc; SSE/multipart and action-callback plumbing are deferred to later iterations.

<h3>Confidence Score: 3/5</h3>

The new code is not safe to merge as-is: the web shim accepts responses from any origin, and a permanently-cached rejected service-start promise can make a service unreachable for the lifetime of the worker.

The web shim's message handler never checks event.origin, so a same-origin sibling frame can inject fake RPC responses. The service trampoline caches a rejected start() Promise forever, meaning a single transient startup failure permanently prevents any rpcMethod on that service from succeeding without a full worker restart. The false idempotency claim in installWebShim would cause silent request leaks in hot-reload scenarios.

packages/plugin-host-shim/src/web.ts needs origin validation and idempotency fixes; packages/plugin-worker-runtime/src/descriptor.ts needs the rejected-promise cleanup in the service trampoline.

<details open><summary><h3>Security Review</h3></summary>

- **Cross-origin response injection** (`packages/plugin-host-shim/src/web.ts`): The `window.addEventListener(\"message\", ...)` handler does not validate `event.origin`. Any frame with a JS reference to the view's window (e.g., a same-origin sibling iframe) can post a crafted `elizaos.shim.response` with a guessable incrementing `id` and resolve a pending RPC call with attacker-controlled data. The `parentOrigin` option only guards outgoing messages.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->6d:Tb7d,## what

three things on the local-inference path:

1. **dflash binary discovery from default user state.** `dflash-server.ts` walks both `ELIZA_STATE_DIR` (isolated app-run state) AND the default user root (`~/.eliza/local-inference/bin/dflash/`). preserves backend preference ordering (cuda > vulkan > rocm > metal > cpu) and picks the durable build over older fused/test builds. fixes the case where the runtime state is isolated per-app but the dflash binary lives in the default user dir.

2. **runtime router wiring in `packages/agent`.** `eliza.ts` adds `ensureLocalInferenceRuntimeHandlers()` which lazy-imports `@elizaos/plugin-local-inference/runtime` and registers the local handlers (TEXT_SMALL, TEXT_LARGE, TEXT_EMBEDDING, RESPONSE_HANDLER, ACTION_PLANNER, etc.) into the runtime instead of relying on static `Plugin.models` exports. `plugin-collector.ts` drops the `ELIZA_DISABLE_LOCAL_EMBEDDINGS=1`-removes-the-whole-plugin code path — the embedding handler now self-disables instead of yanking the whole plugin.

3. **dflash eval gating.** `manifest/validator.ts` requires a passing `evals.dflash` block when a manifest is both `defaultEligible: true` AND ships `files.dflash`. needs-hardware bench (null acceptanceRate or speedup) cannot be marked `passed: true`. matches the pattern used for asr / embedMteb / vadLatency. `manifest/schema.ts` keeps dflash as a per-tier required kernel.

also adds `dflash` to `catalog.ts` BASE_REQUIRED_KERNELS so the runtime probe matches the manifest contract.

## windows ffi build path proven (build-time fixes split into #7988)

after merging recent upstream, the desktop FFI backend requires `libllama.dll` + `libeliza-llama-shim.dll` built via `packages/app-core/scripts/build-llama-cpp-desktop-dylib.mjs` and staged at `~/.eliza/local-inference/bin/llama-cpp/windows-x86_64-<backend>/`.

two windows build-time gaps surfaced and are fixed in #7988:

- `build-llama-cpp-desktop-dylib.mjs` now finds `llama.dll` on win32 (msvc drops the `lib` prefix) and stages it as `libllama.dll` so `desktop-llama-adapter.ts` resolves it.
- `eliza_llama_shim.c` now defines five symbols that were declared in the header and called by the adapter but had no body: `context_detach_drafter`, `context_has_drafter`, `dflash_stats_ex`, `context_handle_memory_pressure`, and the `mtp_stats` adapter alias. msvc was refusing to link the shim with `LNK2019`.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->71:T1508,## Summary

This draft keeps the Linux local-source desktop path current with `origin/develop` and fixes the pieces that were causing the app to wedge on the startup shell, spawn the pill unexpectedly, or fail to deliver local chat cleanly on the Lunar Lake laptop.

Local work is now merged with latest `origin/develop` as of `1b01940387` using merge commits, not rebase.

Notable fixes in this PR:

- `POST /api/agent/start` reports `agentState: "running"` instead of incorrectly setting `paused`; `/api/agent/pause` remains the explicit paused state.
- Electrobun `bootProgress` trusts the API child `/api/health.agentState` when wrapper status is stale, fixing the renderer staying on startup despite the backend being ready.
- The desktop pill window is gated behind the existing pill config instead of spawning unconditionally on Linux.
- Native plugin and app build scripts build/sync the required local workspace packages and shared-brand public assets so local-source builds do not fall through to stale npm/Bun-store artifacts.
- Package/release CI scripts follow the current `packages/scripts/*` layout, the moved `packages/cloud-sdk` workspace, and private workspace packages used only for manifest rewriting.
- Android mobile bundling avoids module-scope TLA in `packages/agent/src/bin.ts` and resolves viem's CJS transitive deps from the matching Bun store package versions instead of incidental top-level symlinks.
- iOS simulator smoke explicitly uses the compatibility runtime instead of requiring a full-Bun xcframework artifact.
- The app Vite config now resolves `@elizaos/app-core/api/ios-local-agent-transport` to local source, so clean CI/mobile checkouts do not require prebuilt `packages/app-core/dist` for that app-core subpath.

## Root Cause

The Linux desktop startup symptoms came from several integration mismatches at once:

- lifecycle start reported `paused`, while runtime health was actually running;
- renderer boot progress read stale wrapper state instead of authoritative API child health;
- the pill window spawned as a second Linux surface on every startup;
- local-source builds could resolve against stale package artifacts when workspace runtime packages/assets were not prepared first;
- after upstream moved scripts/packages, release and tarball CI still referenced old paths;
- Bun mobile bundling exposed viem CJS entrypoints without viem's own dependency graph, and Android module-scope `await` triggered the async `__esm` guard;
- iOS mobile Vite bundling imported an app-core subpath before `packages/app-core/dist` existed in a clean Actions checkout.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->73:T2116,## What

Eliza Cloud is the metered billing rail that sits under a hosted waifu agent. Waifu already exposed signed webhook receivers for credit and inference events, but the emit side was missing. Nothing actually POSTed the credit signals back to waifu, and the one existing provision-complete callback was sent unsigned, so waifu rejected it with a 401. This closes that seam.

This is the correct home for the change: the cloud that the provisioning daemon runs is this monorepo's cloud package (`packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services`), not the old standalone Next.js `app/api` layout.

## Changes

- New `packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/waifu-webhook.ts`: a signed emitter that matches waifu's receiver contract exactly. It computes an HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp and raw body, sends it in the `X-Waifu-Webhook-Signature` header, includes a stable `idempotencyKey` for replay protection, and routes per event kind to the credits or inference receiver. It resolves its target from the environment (`WAIFU_WEBHOOK_URL` + `WAIFU_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and no-ops cleanly when unconfigured, so non-waifu orgs and local or CI environments are unaffected. It never throws, so a webhook delivery problem can never block the billing path.
- `credits.ts`: after a successful deduction crosses the low or depleted threshold, emit `credits.low` or `credits.depleted` to waifu so a hosted agent can downgrade its model tier or pause itself. Fire-and-forget alongside the existing low-credits email.
- `provisioning-jobs.ts`: sign the provision-complete callback with the waifu envelope so the receiver accepts it instead of returning 401.
- `classifyCreditBalance`: pure threshold mapping shared by the billing path so the money-path decision is unit-testable without a database.

## Contract match

Verified byte-for-byte against waifu's receiver (`apps/api/src/routes/v2/webhooks.ts`):
- `sha256=` prefix + HMAC-SHA256 over `` `${timestamp}.${rawBody}` ``
- header `X-Waifu-Webhook-Signature`
- receiver paths `/v2/webhooks/eliza-cloud/credits` and `/v2/webhooks/eliza-cloud/inference`

## Tests

`packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/services/waifu-webhook.test.ts` (13 tests, all passing) locks the signing contract recomputed byte-for-byte against waifu's own scheme, per-kind receiver routing, idempotency key presence, clean no-op when unconfigured, never-throw on delivery error, the credit-status threshold mapping, and the credit and inference payload shapes.

## Scope note

This wires the credit-state money-path emit (low and depleted) and the signed provision callback. The high-volume per-call `inference.spent` emit helper is provided and tested but left unwired by design, since per-inference metering is the separate metering workstream. Do not merge yet.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>
